incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: tokenizer-pool-*/tokenize-container CPU usage > 95% for 3m, 4 pods OOMKilled in last 10m. Paging oncall @anya. Logs and initial context below.

anya (oncall): seeing repeated OOMKill from `tokenizer` process, kernel message shows "Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (tokenizer) score 981". Pods are on nodes ip-10-0-45-*. Node 3 had kernel oom_reaper activity.

sam (sre): joining — can you paste `kubectl describe pod` and `kubectl logs` for a failed pod? Suspect prompt fanout causing many concurrent tokenize jobs.

marta (eng-runtime): past deploy touched batching logic — there was a merge that increased `max_fanout_per_request` to 32. That could blow out CPU for heavy prompts.

anya (oncall): paste: ```kubectl describe pod tokenizer-7f8d9 -n inference``` Events: Back-offRestart, OOMKilled container; Limits: cpu 500m, memory 1Gi; Requests: cpu 200m. Node pressure: CPUHigh. ```kubectl logs tokenizer-7f8d9 --previous``` shows many threads stuck at `tokenize_loop` with repeated regex and normalization work.

sam (sre): logs snippet: ```2026-03-15T03:12:01Z ERROR tokenize.py: heavy prompt: len_tokens=24000 concurrent_fanout=28 cpu_ms=12000``` That CPU_ms number is per-call sum. We're getting a batch of long prompts multiplied by fanout.

josh (support): customer A and B saw 5xx errors for generation endpoints starting ~03:10 UTC. Support ticket opened (INC-8921). Impact: degraded latency >30s, some requests 502.

marta (eng-runtime): interim mitigation: we should reduce `max_fanout_per_request` to 6 and patch default max concurrency per worker. I can push a hotfix config change to staging and then prod.

anya (oncall): doing quick mitigations now: 1) cordon node ip-10-0-45-3 to stop new pods landing there 2) scale up tokenizer pool by +3 nodes (to spread load) 3) temporarily set admission controller to reject requests with prompt length > 8k tokens (soft block).

ops-bot: Executing command: ```kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-3 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-45-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```

sam (sre): also applying a dynamic rate limit at the gateway for `v1/generate` to 30 rps per customer for 10m while we stabilize. Will monitor.

marta (eng-runtime): pushed config to reduce `max_fanout_per_request` -> 6 and rolled to canary 25% across tokenizer pool. Patch: ```diff --git a/runtime/config.yml b/runtime/config.yml
- max_fanout_per_request: 32
+ max_fanout_per_request: 6``` 

anya (oncall): after canary roll, canaries stable for 3 minutes. Evictions stopped on canary nodes. However two other pods still OOMKilled while in backoff. Current customer impact reduced but not fully resolved.

josh (support): updating customer-facing note: "We detected a spike in tokenization CPU usage that caused intermittent failures for generation endpoints. We're throttling large prompts and have rolled a mitigation. We'll follow up once fully restored."

sam (sre): follow up actions I'm taking: - increase pod CPU/memory requests to 1000m/2Gi for tokenizer pool - add liveness probe to restart stuck tokenizers earlier - add alert that watches `concurrent_fanout > 10` per request (derived metric).

marta (eng-runtime): code followups: add heuristic to refuse fanout > 8 for prompts > 4k tokens, and optimize normalization path (remove expensive regex for ASCII-heavy prompts). I'll open PR and tag @anya and @sam.

anya (oncall): handing off to daytime oncall @sam in 30m. Leaving notes: cordoned node ip-10-0-45-3, admission rule in place, rate-limits active, config change rolled to 25% then 100% after validation.

sam (sre): taking the handoff. current state summary: CPU OOMs caused by fanout x long prompts; canary config reduced fanout and saw immediate improvement; nodes cordoned/drained; rate-limits and admission blocks active; increased requests pending rollout; support updated customers. Next: monitor 1h, collect traces to see if KV/prefix cache was evicted causing repetitive compute, and follow up with eng-runtime PR for normalization hotpath.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Recorded incident: incident-ref=INC-1965001234, severity=sev2, start=1965001234

josh (support): leaving note for customers: we will follow up with root cause and permanent mitigation timeline within 24h.

marta (eng-runtime): opened PR #4821 "tokenize: cap fanout and optimize ascii normalize" — will schedule canary tomorrow for perf regression tests.

sam (sre): last check: 10/12 pods healthy, CPU % for tokenizer pool dropped from 94% -> 42% after mitigations. Marking thread for postmortem.

anya (oncall): :thumbsup: thanks team — handing to day.

sam (sre): closing notes: saved logs and heap snapshots to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1965001234/, created follow-up tickets: RT-270 (rate-limiter telemetry), ENG-998 (normalize perf).
